pr.title: Add an InstSimplify for repetitive array expressions
pr.description:
I noticed in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/135068#issuecomment-2569955426 that GVN's implementation of this same transform was quite profitable on the deep-vector benchmark. But of course GVN doesn't run in unoptimized builds, so this is my attempt to write a version of this transform that benefits the deep-vector case and is fast enough to run in InstSimplify.

The benchmark suite indicates that this is effective.
pr.author: saethlin

analysis.summary: Adds InstSimplify::simplify_repeated_aggregate, rewriting an array aggregate of at least five identical *constant* elements (e.g. [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]) into Rvalue::Repeat ([0; 5]). The rewrite is sound only if full const-evaluation results are compared; distinct references to equal referents have different addresses and must not be collapsed. Local/move operands are intentionally not handled (GVN handles those).
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, InstSimplify only called simplify_ref_deref, simplify_ptr_aggregate, and simplify_cast on the Rvalue of an assignment; it had no array-aggregate rewrite. The added logic matches `Rvalue::Aggregate(box AggregateKind::Array(_), fields)`, requires `fields.len() >= 5`, requires the first field to be `Operand::Constant` whose `const_.eval(self.tcx, self.typing_env, first.span)` succeeds, and then requires every field to be an `Operand::Constant` whose const eval equals that first evaluated value. Only then does it replace the Rvalue with `Rvalue::Repeat(Operand::Constant(first.clone()), ty::Const::from_target_usize(...))`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong transformation (explicitly guarded against by the added negative test) is collapsing an array whose elements are *different constant references that point to equal values* into a repeated element, i.e. deciding equality by referent/value rather than by full const-evaluated value including pointer address. The test comment says: `// All of these consts refer to the same value, but the addresses are all different.` and `// It would be wrong to apply the optimization here.` The expected output keeps `_0 = [const equal_referents::A, const equal_referents::B, const equal_referents::C, const equal_referents::D, const equal_referents::E];`. A second wrong variant is treating non-constant `move`/`copy` local operands as equal: the `local` test shows `_0 = [move _2, move _3, move _4, move _5, move _6];` is retained, with the note `// InstSimplify isn't able to see through the move operands, but GVN can.`
analysis.inputDomain: MIR assignments whose Rvalue is an array aggregate of length >= 5 whose fields are all constants: integer literals, const items, `&'static str`, and references. Const evaluation must succeed in the current typing environment. Arrays with fewer than five fields, non-constant operands (locals moved/copied in), or distinct const references are outside the rewritten domain.
analysis.trigger: An array aggregate with at least five fields where every field is `Operand::Constant`, each const-evaluates successfully, and every evaluated value equals the first evaluated value.
preconditions: Every field is `Operand::Constant`; no move/copy local operands
Const eval of every field succeeds under `self.typing_env`
All const-evaluated field values are exactly equal to the first, including pointer provenance/address for reference types
pitfalls: Do not equate references by their referents: constants `&DATA[0]`..`&DATA[4]` have equal pointee values but different addresses, so the array must not become a repeat.
Do not assume non-constant move/copy operands are equal; InstSimplify cannot see through them and the `local` test retains the original aggregate.
Bail out (return) when const eval fails; do not panic or substitute a guessed value.
Respect the `fields.len() < 5` threshold so short arrays are unchanged.
Compare full evaluated const values (`field == Ok(first_val)`), not merely the syntactic constant or type.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a `//@ test-mir-pass: InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg` mir-opt test with `// EMIT_MIR` diff files and CHECK lines. Positive cases: `literals` ([0,0,0,0,0] -> `[const 0_u8; 5]`), `const_items` (distinct const names with equal values -> `[const const_items::A; 5]`), and `strs` (repeated `&str` -> `[const "a"; 5]`). Negative/guard cases: `equal_referents` must keep the five distinct const reference operands, and `local` must keep `[move _2, move _3, move _4, move _5, move _6]`. This distinguishes value equality from address equality and verifies the non-constant-operand boundary.
